.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

FRONTEND_PORT ?= 8080
export FRONTEND_PORT
# Number of jobs `make seed` creates.
N ?= 1000000

COMPOSE := docker compose
# The test stack is a separate compose project (own containers, network and
# volume) built from the base file only, so it publishes no host ports and
# never touches the data of a running `make up` stack.
TEST_COMPOSE := docker compose -p job-dashboard-test -f docker-compose.yml --profile e2e
# Backend unit tests get a third project: own database container and volume,
# so they can run next to `make up` or `make test` without sharing any state.
BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE := docker compose -p job-dashboard-backend-test -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.backend-test.yml

.PHONY: help build up seed test test-backend stop clean

help: ## Show this help
	@grep -E '^[a-z-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk -F ':.*## ' '{printf "  make %-13s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

build: ## Build the Docker images
	$(COMPOSE) build

up: ## Start the app at http://localhost:8080 (override: FRONTEND_PORT=3000 make up)
	$(COMPOSE) up -d --build --wait
	@echo "App running at http://localhost:$(FRONTEND_PORT)"

# Runs inside the backend container of the `make up` stack (`exec`, not `run`),
# so it writes to the database the app is showing. The test stacks are separate
# projects and never see these rows.
seed: ## Add N jobs to the running app (default 1000000; needs `make up` first): make seed N=5000
	@$(COMPOSE) exec -T backend python manage.py seed_jobs "$(N)" || \
	{ echo "make seed needs the app running (make up) and N between 1 and 10000000."; exit 1; }

# exits with the Playwright exit code. A leftover stack from an interrupted run
# is removed first, so every run starts from an empty database. If startup or a
# test fails, the service logs are printed before the stack is removed.
test: ## Run the Playwright E2E tests against a fresh, isolated stack
	@trap '$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans' EXIT; \
	dump_logs() { echo "--- service logs (last 200 lines each) ---"; $(TEST_COMPOSE) logs --no-color --tail 200 db backend frontend; }; \
	$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans && \
	$(TEST_COMPOSE) build && \
	{ $(TEST_COMPOSE) up -d --wait db backend frontend || { dump_logs; exit 1; }; } && \
	{ $(TEST_COMPOSE) run --rm -T e2e || { status=$$?; dump_logs; exit $$status; }; }

# the pytest exit code. `run` starts db (and waits for its healthcheck) through
# depends_on; the backend and frontend services are never started.
test-backend: ## Run the backend unit tests (pytest) against a throwaway Postgres
	@trap '$(BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans' EXIT; \
	$(BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans && \
	$(BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE) build backend-test && \
	$(BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE) run --rm -T backend-test

stop: ## Stop the running containers (data is kept)
	$(COMPOSE) stop

clean: ## Remove containers, networks and volumes of the app and test stacks

	$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans
	$(BACKEND_TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans

# The application stack. No host ports are published here: `make up` adds them
# from docker-compose.override.yml (loaded automatically), while `make test`
# loads only this file, so a busy port on the host cannot fail the tests.
name: job-dashboard

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      # Development default. The database is reachable only inside the compose
      # network; a real deployment supplies its own value.
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

    build:
      context: ./backend
      # Named explicitly: the Dockerfile also has a `test` stage.
      target: runtime
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_HOST: db

      # hostname on a remote machine. Accepted risk: with no login, the Host
      # check is the defence against DNS rebinding (a web page re-pointing its
      # DNS at this machine and calling the API as if it were the app's own
      # page). Small here: a demo database, and port 8080 is open to the
      # network anyway. settings.py keeps a strict default for anything not
      # started through this file. To tighten: DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=localhost make up
      # TODO: before adding auth, set this to the real hostname(s).
      DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS: ${DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-*}
      DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: ${DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:-insecure-dev-only-key}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # The slim Python image has no curl, so the check uses Python itself.
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health/', timeout=2)"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1/"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  # Playwright runner. Behind a profile so `make up` never builds or starts it.
  e2e:
    profiles: [e2e]
    build: ./e2e
    environment:
      BASE_URL: http://frontend
    depends_on:
      frontend:
        condition: service_healthy
    # Chromium needs more shared memory than Docker's 64 MB default, and an
    # init process to reap the helper processes it spawns.
    shm_size: 1gb
    init: true
    # TODO: traces of failed tests stay inside the container and are removed
    # with it. Deferred: a bind mount would leave root-owned files in the clone
    # on Linux. Fix: `docker compose cp` the test-results folder out on failure.

volumes:
  db-data:
# Local-run additions, merged automatically by `docker compose` / `make up`.
# Not used by `make test`.
services:
  frontend:
    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT:-8080}:80"
---GITIGNORE
# Project-specific on purpose. The generic Python template ignored lib/, dist/,
# build/ and var/ at any depth, which would silently drop a source folder such
# as frontend/src/lib from the commit and break a fresh clone.

# Python
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
.pytest_cache/
.mypy_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.coverage
htmlcov/
.venv/
venv/

# Node / frontend / Playwright
node_modules/
/frontend/dist/
/e2e/test-results/
/e2e/playwright-report/

# Local environment and secrets
.env
.env.*

# Editors and OS
/.idea/
.vscode/
.DS_Store

questions.question: When a test fails, Playwright saves a 'trace' (a recording you can replay step by step). Today it is deleted with the container, so a failed `make test` leaves only console text. Should `make test` copy it out on failure?

options.label: Copy out on failure (Recommended)
options.description: Makefile change on the gate path: the e2e container gets a fixed name and no `--rm`; on failure `docker cp` writes e2e/test-results/ (owned by you, not root), then the stack is torn down as now. I verify pass, fail and Ctrl-C reruns. Closes the TODO in docker-compose.yml.

options.label: Leave as is
options.description: No Makefile change, zero added gate risk. The TODO stays; a failure is debugged from the list reporter output and service logs, or by rerunning Playwright by hand.

questions.question: Playwright runs .ts test files without type-checking them, and e2e/ has no tsconfig. A type error in a spec would not fail anything. Add a type check to the e2e image build?

options.label: Add tsc --noEmit (Recommended)
options.description: Adds `typescript` to e2e devDependencies (lockfile regenerated in the Node image), a strict tsconfig.json, and `RUN npx tsc --noEmit` in e2e/Dockerfile. A type error then fails the build, so it fails `make test` deterministically, like the frontend.

# Phase 7 — E2E tests (Playwright)

## Context

Phase 6 is verified. `make test` (the hard gate) currently runs one smoke test that only checks
the page loads. Phase 7 replaces it with the two flows the brief asks for, written so they cannot
flake on an evaluator's machine. Priority order used: the one in the project CLAUDE.md
(1 gate, 2 core correctness, ... 4 code quality / type safety).

Decided by the author: traces stay inside the container (no Makefile change); the e2e image gets
a `tsc --noEmit` step.

## Audit of the current e2e setup (what I found before planning)

| # | Issue | Mechanism (ELI5) | Closed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Retry + unique names = false failure** | `retries: 1` reruns a failed test against the *same* database. Attempt 1 already created "Job A", so attempt 2's create gets a 409 and fails for a reason unrelated to the real bug. | Name has a random suffix per attempt (`randomUUID`), not a fixed string or the test title. Also makes `--repeat-each` and runs against `make up` work. |
| 2 | **Smoke test needs an empty DB** | `getByText('No jobs yet')` is true only if no other test created a job first. Test order then matters. | Smoke test is removed (plan-literal). No new test assumes an empty table. |
| 3 | **"It is gone" can pass on a blank page** | `expect(row).toHaveCount(0)` is true the instant a page starts loading. A negative check proves something only if the thing was there first. | Delete test asserts the row is visible *before* deleting, and does not reload. No optimistic update in the app, so the row leaves only after the server's refetched list arrives. |
| 4 | **Reload can cancel the request** | `page.reload()` right after a click aborts an in-flight PATCH. | Assert the row shows "Running" first (appears only after PATCH + refetch), then reload. |
| 5 | **Specs are not type-checked** | Playwright strips types and runs; `e2e/` has no `tsconfig.json`. | `typescript` dev dependency + strict tsconfig + `tsc --noEmit` in the image build. |
| 6 | **Substring row match** | `getByRole('row', { name })` matches substrings; "Job 1" also matches "Job 10" and Playwright's strict mode then throws. | Fixed-length random suffix at the end of the name; name passed as a string, not a regex. |
| 7 | Traces lost with the container | `run --rm` deletes `/e2e/test-results`. | **Deferred** (author's choice): TODO stays in `docker-compose.yml`. Reason: any fix edits the gate recipe. Fix: fixed container name + `docker cp` on failure. |
| 8 | 5 s assertion timeout | Default `expect` timeout; a cold container on a slow machine can exceed it on first load. | `expect: { timeout: 10_000 }`. A timeout costs time only when a test is failing anyway. |

Not issues (checked): animations (already `reducedMotion: 'reduce'`), stale hidden AntD menus
(`getByRole` ignores hidden elements), parallelism (one spec file = one worker; tests are
independent anyway), fresh DB (`make test` runs `down -v` first).

## Playwright concepts, by analogy

- **Web-first assertion** (`await expect(locator).toBeVisible()`): polls until true or timeout.
  Like an ES test that retries a search until the refresh lands, instead of `sleep(1)`.
- **Locator**: a saved query, re-run on every use, never a stale element handle. Role/label
  locators (`getByRole('button', { name })`) read the accessibility tree, so they survive CSS
  and markup changes and double as an a11y check.
- **Strict mode**: a locator that matches 2 elements throws on action. This is why every
  assertion is scoped to the one row.
- **Retries**: safety net for infrastructure hiccups; a test that needed one is printed as
  `flaky`. "Green" for the exit criterion means 0 flaky, not just exit 0.
- **Trace**: a zip with DOM snapshots, network and console per step; opened with
  `npx playwright show-trace` or trace.playwright.dev.

## Changes

1. **`e2e/tests/helpers.ts`** (new) — small typed functions, no page-object class:
   - `uniqueJobName(label: string): string` → `` `E2E ${label} ${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}` ``
   - `jobRow(page, name): Locator` → `page.getByRole('row', { name })`
   - `createJob(page, name)` → fill `getByLabel('Job name')`, click
     `getByRole('button', { name: 'Create job' })`, `expect(jobRow).toBeVisible()`
   - `statusCell(row, label)` → `row.getByRole('cell', { name: label, exact: true })`
2. **`e2e/tests/jobs.spec.ts`** (new), **delete `smoke.spec.ts`**:
   - *create + change status*: goto `/`, heading visible, `createJob`, row shows `Pending`;
     click `Change status of <name>` → `menuitem` `Running`; row shows `Running`;
     `page.reload()`; row still shows `Running`.
   - *create + delete*: `createJob`; click `Delete <name>` → `button` `Delete` (exact);
     `expect(jobRow).toHaveCount(0)`.
   Locators are the ones recorded in CLAUDE.md Phase 6; each test has a one-line comment on
   what it proves.
3. **`e2e/playwright.config.ts`**: add `expect: { timeout: 10_000 }` with a comment; keep
   `retries: 1`, `trace: 'retain-on-failure'`.
4. **Type check**: `e2e/tsconfig.json` (`strict`, `noEmit`, `types: ["node"]`);
   `typescript` pinned to the frontend's exact version in `e2e/package.json`; lockfile
   regenerated in `node:22-bookworm-slim` (CLAUDE.md command); `RUN` the same check command the
   frontend build uses, placed after `COPY . .` so the Chromium layer stays cached.
5. **`docker-compose.yml`**: reword the trace TODO (what, why deferred, fix) — no behaviour change.
6. **`CLAUDE.md`**: Phase 6 → `[x]`, Phase 7 → `[~]` with a "Built" note; layout (`jobs.spec.ts`,
   `helpers.ts`, `tsconfig.json`); remove "becomes jobs.spec.ts".

No Makefile change. No commit (author commits).

## Verification

- `make test` three times in a row: exit 0, 2 passed, **0 flaky**.
- Flake hunt, once: start the test stack by hand and run
  `npx playwright test --repeat-each 10` in the e2e container (20 runs, same DB) — proves
  name uniqueness and row scoping.
- Type check bites: add a deliberate type error to the spec, `make test` fails at build; revert.
- Break-it (author, per plan): e.g. make `onConfirm` in `JobActions.tsx` a no-op → delete test
  red, `make test` exits non-zero; make `change_status` skip the `Job` save → status test red.
- `make test-backend` still green (untouched, sanity only).

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      # Development default. The database is reachable only inside the compose
      # network; a real deployment supplies its own value.
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      # -h 127.0.0.1 checks over TCP. On first start the image runs a temporary
      # server on the unix socket only; a socket check would pass too early.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U \"$$POSTGRES_USER\" -d \"$$POSTGRES_DB\""]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
      # Named explicitly: the Dockerfile also has a `test` stage.
      target: runtime
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}

## What was built

  - create a job, delete it, its row is gone.

- **CLAUDE.md:** Phase 6 marked done, Phase 7 marked built, plus the layout and two decision rows.

## The Playwright issues, in plain terms

1. **A retry reuses the same database.** `retries: 1` reruns a failed test without resetting anything. Job names are unique, so a fixed name would make the second attempt fail with a 409 and hide the real failure. Each name therefore ends in 8 random hex characters.
2. **"It is gone" is true on a blank page.** `expect(row).toHaveCount(0)` passes the instant a page starts loading. The delete test first waits for the row to be visible, then deletes, and does not reload. The app has no optimistic update, so the row only leaves once the server's new list arrives.
3. **A reload can cancel a request in flight.** The status test waits for "Running" in the row before `page.reload()`. That text only appears after the PATCH succeeded and the list was fetched again.
4. **A locator that matches two things throws.** `getByRole('row', { name })` matches by substring, so "Job 1" would also match "Job 10". The random part has a fixed length and comes last, so one name is never the start of another.
5. **Assertions poll, they do not sleep.** `await expect(x).toBeVisible()` re-checks until true or timeout, like retrying an ES search until the refresh lands. A longer timeout only costs time when a test is failing anyway.
6. **Playwright does not type-check.** It strips the types and runs the file, which is why the check is a separate build step.
